findings.evidence: `Ball.lean:44` sets the stronger assumptions, while the proofs at lines 53-55, 64-66, and 74-78 use only `dist_eq_norm`, `norm_smul`, and `norm_pos_iff`; Mathlib has the analogous scaling API `DilationEquiv.smulTorsor` under `[NormedDivisionRing 𝕜] [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜 E] [NormSMulClass 𝕜 E]` in `Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Affine/AddTorsor.lean:244`.
findings.fix: State these three lemmas under the weaker Mathlib-style assumptions, e.g. `[NormedDivisionRing 𝕜] [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜 E] [NormSMulClass 𝕜 E]`; keep the later harmonic lemmas specialized to real inner product spaces.
findings.issue: The shared assumptions for `preimage_const_add_smul_ball`, `preimage_const_add_smul_closedBall`, and `preimage_const_add_smul_sphere` require `[NormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]`, but the proofs only use scalar norm multiplication and cancellation by a nonzero scalar norm.

summary: The new preimage API is useful but is stated with stronger scalar and space assumptions than the standard Mathlib level for these metric scaling facts.
